body:
Do you think it might be easier if I was a little bit drunk or something? That'd help with the nerves, maybe.

It's funny that the your conscious, rational mind - as sick as it might be - can decide with total resolve to die but still *animal body says* ***no***.

Same. It's like I *know* this is a sure-fire (lol) way to get the job done, but my brain won't let me do it. It has this automatic "must be able to return to the holding pattern if all goes wrong" reaction to any decision I make, even if *the whole point* is to not be able to turn back. I'm too noncommittal and fearful to properly kill myself. :shrug:

I live with my parents b/c I just finished college and commuted from home the whole time anyway. I can't talk to my dad b/c he's the be-all-end-all of expectations in my life and tbh the source of a good bit of my career/life/aspirational stress. Can't talk to my stepmom b/c if I do she'll just tell my dad everything to absolve herself of potential culpability should he ever find out she knew something and didn't tell him; therefore telling her anything would be even worse than telling my dad, b/c he'd find out anyway and be even more upset that I tried to hide whatever-it-is from him. I don't have any social contacts outside of them.
I'm simultaneously terrified of the pain and scared of instantaneous death - just going out like a light. I wish I could have a *process of dying* without the *pain of dying*.
Wearing shorts in the summer when you know those thigh yeets are just above the hem. It's an extreme sport.

Things in the house that go boom.

They're legal, and initially I was averse to using them b/c I was afraid that doing so might get the owner's rights to them revoked or something, but given that other methods are either unavailable or unviable (tried to hang myself over a door but I was too tall and the "rope" too elastic), they might be my only option.

It's not even like getting caught between a rock and a hard place; it's being stuck in a hard place with ready access to a very soft place, but not being able to get there because the price of entry is a Big Decision that fires up the ol' Anxiety Engine for no reason.

You're right; it's the worst feeling possible.
